record.paper_title: Five open problems in theory of quantum information
record.original_question: For an N-dimensional complex Hilbert space H_N, construct symmetric informationally complete positive-operator-valued measurements (SIC POVMs) in an infinite sequence of dimensions N_1, N_2, N_3, .... Concretely, for each dimension N in the sequence, find N^2 vectors |ψ_j⟩ in H_N whose squared overlaps satisfy |⟨ψ_j|ψ_k⟩|^2 = (N δ_jk + 1)/(N + 1) for all j,k = 1,...,N^2, so that the associated projectors form a simplex in the N^2−1 dimensional set of density matrices.

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Construct SIC POVMs in an infinite sequence of dimensions,N1, N2, N3, . . . Setup. A symmetric informationally complete positive operator valued measure [15, 16] associated with an N-dimensional complex Hilbert spaceHN is given by a set ofN2 vectors∣ψj⟩∈ HN satisfying the following overlap relations, ∣⟨ψj∣ψk⟩∣2= N δjk+ 1 N+ 1 , j, k = 1, . . . , N2.

However, in spite of a considerable research effort [27–31], the general conjecture of Zauner remains unproven. Finding a family of SICs in any infinite sequence of dimensions could become a decisive step in this direction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_N$ denote an $N$-dimensional complex Hilbert space. A symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measure (SIC-POVM) in dimension $N$ is a collection of $N^2$ unit vectors $|\psi_1angle, \ldots, |\psi_{N^2}angle \in \mathcal{H}_N$ satisfying the overlap relations
$$|\langle \psi_j | \psi_k angle|^2 =  rac{N\delta_{jk}+1}{N+1}, \qquad j,k = 1, \ldots, N^2,$$
so that the rank-one projectors $\Pi_j = |\psi_jangle\langle\psi_j|$ form a regular simplex inside the $(N^2-1)$-dimensional convex set of density matrices on $\mathcal{H}_N$, and the rescaled operators $ rac{1}{N}\Pi_j$ form a POVM that is informationally complete.

Problem: Exhibit an infinite sequence of dimensions $N_1 < N_2 < N_3 < \cdots$ together with an explicit construction that, for every $i$, produces a SIC-POVM in $\mathcal{H}_{N_i}$. Equivalently, prove that there exist infinitely many integers $N \ge 2$ for which a SIC-POVM in dimension $N$ exists, and provide such a construction.
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of SIC-POVMs in all finite dimensions (Zauner's conjecture) remains open. Exact solutions are known in many specific dimensions (e.g., 2–24, 28, 30, 31, 35, 37, 39, 43, 48, 124, and additional sporadic cases extended through 2024–2025), and conjectural infinite-family constructions exist (e.g., Kopp's construction for odd primes $d\equiv 2\pmod 3$ contingent on a Stark-type conjecture about real units in ray class fields). However, no unconditional proof providing SIC-POVMs in an infinite sequence of dimensions has yet been published as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: SIC POVMs and Zauner's Conjecture – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Despite extensive numerical and analytic evidence, Zauner's conjecture and the existence of SIC-POVMs in all dimensions remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of SIC-POVMs in all dimensions is an open problem.

status_evidence.title: SIC-POVMs and the Stark Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: A conjectural construction of Heisenberg SIC-POVMs in infinitely many dimensions d=5,11,17,23,29,41,... assuming Stark-type conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Infinite-family constructions are conditional on number-theoretic conjectures, not unconditional.

status_evidence.title: SIC-POVM - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Exact solutions known in dimensions 2-24, 28, 30, 31, 35, 37, 39, 43, 48, 124, with no general proof.
status_evidence.claim: Only finitely many specific dimensions have verified exact SIC-POVMs.
